clue.text: Not be punished for light doze?

definitions.meaning: to escape a penalty, as a defendant acquitted in court does
to drop off to sleep, the start of a light doze

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both escaping punishment and nodding off to sleep, two quite separate idioms.

clue.text: Journalist is working with inventor

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A reporter is collaborating with an inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and light bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Edison is a famous example of an inventor.

clue.text: Old-time record, we hear

parts.note: a record of past times passed on by speech, so it is heard not read, rather than a vinyl disc

explanation.definitionFit: History gathered from spoken memories is an account of olden times that one hears.

clue.text: Very good quality desserts, perhaps, served up flambeed?

annotationWithheld.why: Very good quality desserts, perhaps, served up flambeed? (5-4): TARTS reversed inside FIRE, but 'flambeed' must give FIRE and also signal the containment, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Very good quality desserts, perhaps, served up flambeed?

clue.text: Further wait after public transport setback

indicators.note: the waiting word is placed after the reversed vehicle
set back read as turned backwards, so the vehicle's name is read in reverse

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport
to wait at table is to serve

explanation.surface: A frustrated commuter faces a longer wait after a delayed bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Further' looks like an adjective at the start of the surface, but here it is the verb meaning to promote.
explanation.definitionFit: To subserve is to promote or help along, so it is a formal synonym of the verb further.

clue.text: Dog a female left on leash?

parts.note: she refers to a female
a tie is something that ties, like a leash

explanation.surface: A female dog left tied on a lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltie is a Shetland sheepdog, a breed of dog.

clue.text: The sound of spring is dull? Not right

indicators.note: says the following letter is removed

parts.note: boring means dull

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a dull spring sound is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' is not the season but a coiled spring; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Boing is the comic noise of a coiled spring bouncing.

clue.text: Mischief maker regularly infiltrating New Left

indicators.note: takes every other letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: A troublemaker steadily infiltrates the New Left political movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infiltrating' is a link; the New Left was a 1960s radical movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves in folklore play tricks, so a mischief maker describes one.

clue.text: Conquered queen has gone and disappeared

indicators.note: says the queen letters are removed from the conquered word

parts.note: vanquished means conquered

explanation.surface: A defeated queen has left and vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanished means gone from sight, the same as disappeared.

clue.text: I greased wheels in dispute

indicators.note: wheels as a verb means turns around, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mechanic greased the wheels during an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' looks like a noun being greased but is the anagram signal; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute is to argue or differ, the same verb sense as to disagree.

clue.text: Child wearing cool togs to begin with

parts.note: wearing clothes means being in them
a fan cools you down, so the word stands for the cooling device

indicators.note: says only the opening letter of togs is used

explanation.surface: A child wearing cool clothes, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool' is FAN, the thing that cools; 'togs' is British slang for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a very young child, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pork to be served with pork pie: does it matter?

parts.note: a sow is a female pig, the source of pork
a pork pie hat is a flat-crowned style of hat

explanation.surface: A butcher's menu pairs pork with a pork pie, and asks if it matters.
explanation.walkthrough: A pork pie is a British cold pastry snack, but here it is the hat style.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word retort is a shrugging way of asking whether something is of any importance.

clue.text: Extremely tense in spoken language exam

indicators.note: signals that the words are heard rather than written, so we want a soundalike

parts.note: a test in the Thai language would be a Thai test

explanation.surface: Someone is as nervous as can be in an oral language exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken' looks like the type of exam, but it signals the soundalike of 'Thai test'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tightest is the superlative of tight, and extremely tense means stretched or strained to the utmost.

clue.text: A visit's not straightforward after one's mislaid in Orient Express?

definitions.text: A visit's not straightforward after one's mislaid in Orient Express?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the shortened train
lost, so the letter for one is removed from the train

parts.note: the Orient Express is a famous train
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are rearranged rather than kept in order

explanation.surface: A trip on the Orient Express gets complicated after someone loses a document.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAIN less I gives TRAN; 'not straightforward' turns A VISITS into SITVISA.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit to pass through a country while journeying is exactly what one might lose on a long train trip.

clue.text: One with important theatrical role, a celebrity, recoiling in shock

indicators.note: the reversed phrase is placed inside the word for shock

parts.note: to shock or astonish is to stagger

indicators.note: springing back, so the phrase a celebrity is read backwards

parts.note: a big name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A star of the stage, a famous name, reels back in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recoiling' looks like a celebrity flinching, but it signals reading the phrase backwards; 'One with important theatrical role' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The person running the backstage side of a production holds a vital role in the theatre.

clue.text: Flower, one attached to branch I put in water

indicators.note: places the run of pieces inside the water word

parts.note: aqua is Latin for water
I is the Roman numeral one
a leg is a limb or branch

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a flower and a branch in a vase of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attached to' is a link joining I and LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquilegia is a garden flower, also called columbine.

clue.text: Underground worker nursing sick trader

indicators.note: holding inside, as one nurses something close

parts.note: a miner works underground
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A miner looks after an ailing shopkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliner makes and sells hats, so is a kind of trader.

clue.text: United Nations is now working with press to achieve distinction

indicators.note: when something is reworked its letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: The UN is now working with the media to make a name for itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working with' joins the press to the fodder: UN, IS NOW and PRESS are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from a knight earning his spurs, meaning to prove oneself and gain honour.

clue.text: Somewhere to meet me in Missouri?

definitions.text: Somewhere to meet me in Missouri?

parts.words: Somewhere to meet me in Missouri?
parts.note: recalls the film and song Meet Me in ..., set at the 1904 World's Fair in a Missouri city

explanation.definitionFit: The city is in Missouri and is named in the classic Judy Garland musical's title.

clue.text: Worker has business with elderly person — heart's not in it

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: an oldie is an old person

explanation.surface: A labourer runs a firm with an old man who lacks enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A coolie was an unskilled labourer in Asia; the word is now considered offensive.

clue.text: Be cooperative, and perform service in court

definitions.meaning: to go along with others and work together
in a ball game you put the ball into play with a serve on the court

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to cooperate, while literally it means starting a ball game.

clue.text: Learners in top class at new comprehensive

indicators.note: places the learners inside the top class

parts.note: A1 means first-class; read as letters it is AI
L is the learner plate, so two Ls for learners

explanation.surface: Students in the top set at a new comprehensive school.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British state secondary school; here it is the adjective. 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: All-in means inclusive or covering everything, so it matches comprehensive.

clue.text: Sunscreen? Large amount applied when touring island

indicators.note: going round, so the first pair of words encloses the island letter

parts.note: a lot is a large amount
a cream applied is put on

explanation.surface: Lots of sunscreen is applied when holidaying on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunscreen?' has a question mark because sunscreen is just one example of the definition; 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunscreen is one example of a cream rubbed on the skin, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Circus performer, maybe, got plate spinning

indicators.note: turning round, so the plate word is read backwards

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: A circus act keeps a plate spinning on a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' fits the circus plate-spinner, but it reverses LAMINA.
explanation.definitionFit: A performing lion or elephant is a beast, hence 'maybe' for an example.

clue.text: Say it's to be written after maiden name

indicators.note: the example word is written after the maiden letter

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
eg means for example, or say

explanation.surface: A bride says her maiden name will be written down.
explanation.definitionFit: Meg is a girl's name, short for Margaret.

clue.text: Clumsy guy in lane almost becoming confused

indicators.note: being jumbled up, so the letters are rearranged
almost the whole word, so the last letter of lane is dropped

explanation.surface: An awkward man in a lane gets disoriented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LANE to LAN; GUY IN LAN is then shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungainly means awkward and lacking grace, a direct synonym of clumsy.

clue.text: Robbers in gangs, concealing gear

indicators.note: hiding inside, so the gear word goes within the gangs word

parts.note: bands are groups or gangs
a rig is a set of gear or equipment

explanation.surface: Robbers in gangs hiding their equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of the container but is only a link word here; the container signal is 'concealing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigands are bandits who rob travellers, so the plural matches robbers.

clue.text: Surprised a puzzle's solved finally

parts.note: a maze is a puzzle of paths

indicators.note: takes just the closing letter of solved

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised that a puzzle finally got solved.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazed means astonished or taken aback, a synonym of surprised.
